name: v0
best_for: Prompt to React UI you can copy out
tradeoffs: Produces clean React and Tailwind UI quickly and syncs with GitHub, but it is a credit meter rather than a flat fee. Long iteration sessions burn credits fast, and its strength is the front end, not a full backend.
long_term: Export to your own repo early (it creates a branch per chat and can open pull requests) so the code outlives the subscription. Best used as the design-to-code step that feeds a real codebase.
watch_out: Billed separately from Vercel hosting
Monthly credits roll over once and expire after about 65 days
Plans were reshuffled in 2026: Team renamed Plus in July, personal accounts converted to team workspaces in October
Moved from v0.dev to v0.app in January 2026
pricing_notes: Free: about $5 of monthly credits and 7 messages a day. Plus about $30 per user per month with $30 of credits; Business about $100. Checked November 2026.

name: Stitch
best_for: Prompt to screen designs, exportable to code
tradeoffs: Fast way to get screen designs from a prompt or sketch, with export toward code and design tools. Output is a starting point: layouts still need real component structure and consistency.
long_term: It comes from Google Labs, so features and limits can change with little notice. Export what you like instead of treating it as your design source of truth.
watch_out: Experimental product: limits and availability may change
Generated screens are not a design system
Check generation limits on the current plan page

name: Magic Patterns
best_for: Prompt to editable UI with design variations
tradeoffs: Strong at producing several editable variations from a prompt or screenshot, aimed at product teams. It is a design tool first, not a full app builder.
long_term: A smaller company than the big builders, so keep exported code and designs in your own repo.
watch_out: Free tier limits the number of generations
Verify export options and pricing before committing

name: Lovable
best_for: Prompt a full web app with no code
tradeoffs: Best prompt-to-app experience for non-coders, with GitHub sync, one-click publishing and a built-in cloud backend. Cost is credit-based plus runtime usage, so complex projects and repeated fix attempts burn credits quickly.
long_term: You can sync to GitHub and own the code, but long debugging loops are expensive on a credit meter, so many builders move to an editor or coding agent once the app grows. Reported to use TanStack Start for new projects since May 2026.
watch_out: Credits are shared with no per-user guardrails on Pro; Business adds per-member limits
Cloud function, database and storage usage can add runtime charges
Unused credits keep their original expiry
No native app store publishing
pricing_notes: Free: 5 daily credits, capped at 30 a month (official docs). Paid from about $25 a month; annual billing arrived mid-2026; top-ups reported at $15 per 50 credits. Credit counts per plan differ between sources, so confirm on lovable.dev.

name: Bolt.new
best_for: Full-stack app in the browser from a prompt
tradeoffs: Runs a full-stack dev environment in the browser, so you go from prompt to deployed app fast. Pricing is raw tokens, which are hard to predict as a project grows.
long_term: Great for prototypes. Larger codebases mean more context on every prompt, so token cost climbs; move the code to GitHub and an editor when it gets serious.
watch_out: Unused paid tokens roll over only one extra month and are forfeited on cancel
The free tier has a daily cap as well as a monthly one
Hosting and database usage are limited per plan
pricing_notes: Free: 1M tokens a month with a 300K daily cap. Pro about $25 a month for 10M tokens; Teams about $30 per member. Checked October 2026.

name: Replit Agent
best_for: Build and host from a phone browser
tradeoffs: The one builder here that creates, runs and hosts the app in a single browser tab, which is why it works from a phone. Billing is effort-based, so a request's price is known only after it finishes, though it asks for confirmation before paid actions.
long_term: Great for getting something live and iterating without local setup. Costs are harder to predict at scale, and the app lives in Replit's environment unless you export to GitHub.
watch_out: Even Plan Mode chats with the Agent are billable
Set a spending cap to avoid overage once credits run out
The effort-based pricing rollout caused user backlash; re-check before building a business on it
Free Mode covers everyday work on paid plans, but Power and Max modes spend credits
pricing_notes: Core about $25 a month including about $20 of credits (June 2026 figures). Extra usage is billed once credits run out unless capped. Cloud prices were cut in August 2026.

name: Claude Code
best_for: Agent that edits a real codebase
tradeoffs: Works on a real codebase with your own tools and git history, so you keep full ownership and control. It needs comfort with a terminal or editor, and heavy use is bounded by plan usage caps or API cost.
long_term: Pair it with git from day one. The better your tests and written project notes, the better any coding agent performs month after month.
watch_out: Usage limits depend on your plan or API spend; check current Anthropic pricing
Review diffs, because an agent can change many files at once
Terminal-first, which is harder from a phone

name: Cursor
best_for: AI-first editor for keeping control of the code
tradeoffs: An AI-first editor that keeps you in control of real code. AI usage is metered, and the metering has changed several times.
long_term: Third-party coverage reports a SpaceX acquisition completed in August 2026, Auto mode metered from August, a plan restructure on October 12, and OpenAI planning to end its model supply to Cursor from November 12, 2026. Treat model availability and pricing as moving targets.
watch_out: The old $20 Pro plan is reported to keep working for existing subscribers while new customers see a new ladder
Which models are included may change
Confirm current pricing and models at cursor.com
pricing_notes: Pro was $20 a month; reports say new customers moved to a ladder starting around $30 a month in October 2026. Verify before paying.

name: Aider
best_for: Open-source pair programmer in the terminal
tradeoffs: Cheap and transparent: you pay only for model API usage, and every change is a git commit you can undo. Terminal-only, with no hand-holding.
long_term: Open source with no vendor lock-in, and it works with many model providers, so you can switch models as prices change.
watch_out: API costs can add up on large repos
Requires comfort with git and a terminal
Pace depends on its maintainers; check recent releases

name: Supabase
best_for: Postgres, auth and storage in one
tradeoffs: Postgres plus auth, storage and realtime in one dashboard, with real SQL and no proprietary database. You must understand Row Level Security, or your data can be exposed.
long_term: Portable: it is standard Postgres, so you can export or self-host. Pro adds daily backups and removes inactivity pausing.
watch_out: Free projects pause after about a week of low activity, and the restore window is limited
Free tier: 2 active projects, 500MB database, 50k monthly active users, 5GB egress
Reported: new projects created after May 30, 2026 need explicit Postgres grants for Data API access, and existing free projects from October 30, 2026
Turn on Row Level Security before launch
pricing_notes: Pro about $25 a month per project (2026 sources). Checked November 2026.

name: Firebase
best_for: Realtime data and hosting from Google
tradeoffs: Fast to start with realtime data, auth and hosting from Google. The NoSQL data model and proprietary APIs make it harder to leave and weaker for relational queries.
long_term: Costs scale with reads and writes, so a chatty app can get expensive. Model your data around the queries you will run.
watch_out: Set budget alerts early
Security rule mistakes expose data
Migrating off Firestore later is real work

name: Neon
best_for: Serverless Postgres that scales to zero
tradeoffs: Serverless Postgres that scales to zero and branches databases instantly, which is great for preview environments. Cold starts can add latency on idle databases.
long_term: Neon was acquired by Databricks in 2025; check the current roadmap and terms. It stays standard Postgres, so leaving is easy.
watch_out: Cold-start delay after idle on small plans
Check free-tier compute and storage limits
Connection pooling settings matter on serverless hosts

name: PocketBase
best_for: Whole backend in a single file
tradeoffs: One small executable gives you a database, auth, file storage and an admin UI. Excellent for small apps, but it is SQLite on one server, so scaling out is a limit.
long_term: You host it yourself, so backups, updates and uptime are yours. It is pre-1.0, so expect breaking changes between versions.
watch_out: Back up the data folder regularly
Not designed for horizontal scale
Upgrades can break between pre-1.0 versions

name: Convex
best_for: Reactive backend written in TypeScript
tradeoffs: A reactive backend where queries update live and everything is TypeScript. It is a proprietary model with its own concepts rather than SQL.
long_term: An open-source backend exists, but most people use the hosted service. Moving off means rewriting data access.
watch_out: Learn its query and mutation model first
Lock-in is higher than with Postgres options
Watch usage-based costs as data grows

name: Turso
best_for: Tiny SQLite databases at the edge
tradeoffs: SQLite-compatible (libSQL) databases that are cheap and quick to create, even one per user. Fewer features than Postgres and a smaller ecosystem.
long_term: A good fit for read-heavy apps and per-tenant databases.
watch_out: SQLite behaviour differs from Postgres
Check limits and pricing for the number of databases
Smaller community and tooling

name: Clerk
best_for: Drop-in sign-in screens and user management
tradeoffs: Beautiful drop-in sign-in components and user management in minutes. You pay by monthly active user, and your users live in Clerk.
long_term: Migrating users away later is possible but takes effort, and costs grow with active users.
watch_out: The free tier is limited by monthly active users
Use webhooks to sync users to your own database
Login uptime depends on a third party

name: Better Auth
best_for: Open-source auth you own
tradeoffs: An open-source TypeScript auth library that runs inside your app against your own database. More setup, and you own security updates.
long_term: No per-user fees or vendor lock-in. It is a relatively young project, so APIs change.
watch_out: You are responsible for upgrades and security patches
Younger than established options
Check plugin maturity for features like organizations

name: Stripe
best_for: Cards and subscriptions
tradeoffs: The most complete payments platform, with excellent docs. By default you remain the seller of record, so global sales tax is your job.
long_term: Stripe Managed Payments, built from the Lemon Squeezy acquisition and reported generally available since April 2026, makes Stripe the legal seller for eligible transactions and handles indirect tax. It is not available in every country.
watch_out: Check Stripe's supported countries before building around it
Managed Payments is separate from Stripe Tax
Plan for disputes and chargebacks
pricing_notes: Standard processing is a percentage plus a fixed fee per charge; Managed Payments adds its own fee. Confirm current rates on stripe.com.

name: Lemon Squeezy
best_for: Sell digital products with tax handled
tradeoffs: A merchant of record that handled global sales tax for digital products, but it is winding down.
long_term: Reported: it will stop processing payments on March 31, 2027 and is steering customers to Stripe Managed Payments, which is not available in every country Lemon Squeezy supported.
watch_out: Do not start new projects on it
If you use it, plan a migration (Stripe Managed Payments, Paddle or another merchant of record)
Check country eligibility for the replacement

name: Flutterwave
best_for: Cards, bank transfers and mobile money across many African markets
tradeoffs: Strong African coverage including mobile money in several markets. Integration can be fiddlier than Stripe, and which payment methods work differs by country and currency.
long_term: Pick it when your customers are in supported African markets; outside them it adds little over a global processor. Merchant accounts are tied to your business country, so check eligibility early.
watch_out: Not every payment method works in every country, so check the methods table per currency
Some payment methods need approval for merchants based outside that market
Test mode behaves differently from live mobile money

name: Paystack
best_for: Payments for businesses in supported African markets
tradeoffs: Clean developer experience and owned by Stripe since 2020. It covers a limited set of African markets, so confirm your country is supported before building around it.
long_term: Settlement currency and timing depend on your country and account type.
watch_out: Verify supported countries and currencies
Payout currency and timing vary
Mobile money availability varies by market

name: Resend
best_for: Email API made for developers
tradeoffs: A simple API and React Email templates make transactional email painless. It focuses on sending, not full marketing automation.
long_term: Deliverability is on you: set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC on your own domain.
watch_out: Free tier has sending caps
Verify your domain before launch
Handle bounces and complaints

name: OpenRouter
best_for: One API key for many models
tradeoffs: One key and one API for many models, so switching as prices change is easy. It adds a layer between you and the provider, and availability and latency vary by model.
long_term: Handy for comparing models, but a direct provider account can be cheaper at volume.
watch_out: Per-model pricing differs, so set spending limits
Provider outages and model retirements still affect you
Data handling differs by upstream provider

name: Gemini API
best_for: Google models with a free tier to start
tradeoffs: Strong multimodal and long-context features, with a free tier that is handy for prototyping. Quotas and model names change often.
long_term: Plan for model versions being replaced over time.
watch_out: Check whether free-tier data may be used to improve products
Rate limits are tighter on the free tier
Pin model versions and test upgrades

name: Claude API
best_for: Text and tool-using models
tradeoffs: Strong at coding and tool use, with prompt caching and batch discounts to control cost. Usage-based, so cost scales with traffic.
long_term: Models are retired on a schedule, so pin a version and plan upgrades.
watch_out: Set budget and rate limits on your key
Never put the key in front-end code
Handle rate limit errors with retries

name: ElevenLabs
best_for: Realistic voices and speech
tradeoffs: Very natural voices and voice cloning. Credit pricing makes long audio expensive, and cloning needs consent.
long_term: Check commercial-use terms for your plan before shipping a product on it.
watch_out: Credits are consumed per character
Voice cloning requires consent and has usage policies
Commercial licence terms depend on plan

name: fal
best_for: Fast image and video model APIs
tradeoffs: Fast hosted image, video and audio models behind a simple API. Pay per generation, so costs are unpredictable if users generate freely.
long_term: Models come and go, so avoid hard-wiring one.
watch_out: Add per-user generation limits
Review each model's licence for commercial use
Model availability changes

name: Expo
best_for: React Native apps without native setup
tradeoffs: The fastest route to a real iOS and Android app with React and TypeScript, with cloud builds and over-the-air updates. Custom native code means leaving the easy path.
long_term: App store rules, not the framework, are the real bottleneck.
watch_out: Apple and Google developer accounts are paid and required
Cloud build queues are slower on free tiers
Some native modules need a development build instead of Expo Go

name: Capacitor
best_for: Wrap a web app as a native app
tradeoffs: Wraps an existing web app as an iOS or Android app with native plugins. It is still a web view, so heavy animation feels less native.
long_term: Good when you already have a web app and want store presence.
watch_out: Stores may reject thin web wrappers
Plugin maintenance varies
Test on real devices

name: FlutterFlow
best_for: Visual builder for mobile apps
tradeoffs: A visual builder that produces Flutter apps with a polished UI kit. You live in Flutter and Dart, and exported code can be hard to maintain by hand.
long_term: Fine for MVPs; consider how you would maintain it if you leave the builder.
watch_out: Code export is limited to paid plans (check current terms)
Complex logic is clunky in visual form
Dart skills differ from React

name: Phaser
best_for: The classic 2D browser game framework
tradeoffs: Mature, with a huge community and many examples, ideal for 2D browser games. Code-first, with no built-in editor.
long_term: You need JavaScript or TypeScript skills, but the ecosystem is deep.
watch_out: Mobile browser performance varies
Check licences for art and audio
Plan how to package for app stores

name: KAPLAY
best_for: Playful JavaScript game library
tradeoffs: A friendly small library for quick 2D games, ideal for jams and learning. Smaller ecosystem and less suited to large projects.
long_term: It continues the community fork of Kaboom.js, so many older Kaboom tutorials still apply.
watch_out: Smaller community than Phaser
Large games may outgrow it
Check recent release activity

name: Rosebud
best_for: Describe a game, play it in the browser
tradeoffs: Describe a game and play it in the browser, with AI-generated assets. Quick, fun prototypes, but limited control and platform lock-in.
long_term: Treat it as a sketchpad for ideas unless export terms suit you.
watch_out: Check export and ownership terms
Generation is credit-based
Quality varies on complex mechanics

name: WXT
best_for: Modern framework for browser extensions
tradeoffs: A modern Vite-based framework that targets Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari from one codebase, with HMR and publishing helpers. Still pre-1.0, so APIs can change between releases.
long_term: Reported actively maintained through 2026 (a release in August 2026) and named the default pick for new extensions by several 2026 comparisons.
watch_out: Pre-1.0 versions can bring breaking changes
Store review has strict permission rules
Chrome Web Store discovery is slow without promotion

name: Plasmo
best_for: Batteries-included extension framework
tradeoffs: React-first with the most tutorials and a smooth first run, but described by WXT's comparison and other sources as in maintenance mode.
long_term: Reported: latest npm release was in May 2025 (per an October 2026 comparison), and an older Parcel version blocks Tailwind v4. Fine for an existing app, risky as a fresh pick.
watch_out: Little active feature development reported
Build tooling lags behind Vite-based options
Migrating to WXT or Extension.js is possible but takes effort

name: n8n
best_for: Visual workflows you can self-host
tradeoffs: Powerful visual workflow builder you can self-host. Its licence is source-available (fair-code), not open source, with limits on reselling it as a service.
long_term: Cloud pricing counts workflow executions. Self-hosting is cheap but real ops work.
watch_out: Read the Sustainable Use Licence if you plan to resell
Protect credentials stored in workflows
Self-hosted upgrades can break workflows

name: Val Town
best_for: Write a function, get a live URL
tradeoffs: Write a function and get a URL, a cron job or an email handler instantly. Perfect for small scripts and glue, not large apps.
long_term: Great for quick automations, with a vendor-specific runtime.
watch_out: Runtime limits apply on free plans
Code depends on the platform's runtime
Check limits before relying on it

name: Activepieces
best_for: Open-source automation builder
tradeoffs: An open-source-core automation builder with a friendly UI. Fewer ready-made integrations than the biggest players.
long_term: Self-hosting works, but you maintain it.
watch_out: Smaller integration library
Some features are paid editions
Self-hosting means ops work

name: Trigger.dev
best_for: Background jobs for long tasks
tradeoffs: Run long background jobs and scheduled tasks in TypeScript without timeouts, with retries and logs. One more service to learn and pay for.
long_term: Replaces fragile queues in serverless apps.
watch_out: Check free-tier run limits
Queue delays can occur
Self-hosting needs ops

name: Astro
best_for: Content sites that load fast
tradeoffs: Ships very little JavaScript so content sites load fast, and mixes React, Vue and Svelte. Not the first pick for highly interactive app-like products.
long_term: Pair it with a host such as Cloudflare, Netlify or Vercel.
watch_out: Content collections and islands have a learning curve
Major upgrades need migration work
Interactive dashboards fit other frameworks better

name: Framer
best_for: Design and publish a site visually
tradeoffs: Design and publish a polished site visually, with animations and a CMS. You are tied to Framer hosting and pricing, with no source code export.
long_term: Great for marketing sites; weak if you may later need custom backend logic.
watch_out: Pricing is per site
No true code export
CMS limits on lower plans

name: Vercel
best_for: Push to deploy for Next.js and more
tradeoffs: The smoothest deploy experience for Next.js, with preview URLs on every push. Usage-based pricing can surprise you as traffic grows.
long_term: The Hobby plan is for non-commercial personal use only. Any commercial project needs Pro, about $20 per user per month with $20 of included usage.
watch_out: Moving a client or paid project off Hobby is required by the terms
Bandwidth, function and image optimization overages are metered
v0 is billed separately from Vercel
pricing_notes: Hobby: free, non-commercial. Pro: about $20 per user per month plus $20 usage credit. Checked November 2026.

name: Netlify
best_for: Simple static and serverless hosting
tradeoffs: Friendly static and serverless hosting, and the free tier allows commercial use within limits.
long_term: Moved to credit-based usage; reported flat $20 Pro with unlimited team members from April 2026 (verify).
watch_out: Free tier reported to have a hard credit limit with no overages
Credit systems make cost harder to predict
Confirm current pricing

name: Cloudflare Workers + Pages
best_for: Free-tier hosting on a global network, static or full-stack
tradeoffs: A global network with a generous free tier, and static asset requests are free. More config-driven than Vercel or Netlify.
long_term: Cloudflare now recommends Workers with Static Assets for new projects and focuses new features there. Pages keeps working and has a documented migration path.
watch_out: Workers serve static assets before your code by default, unlike Pages Functions
Frameworks like Next.js need an adapter
Check Workers CPU and size limits

name: Render
best_for: Hosting for web services and workers
tradeoffs: Simple hosting for web services, workers, cron jobs and Postgres, with a Heroku-like feel. Free instances sleep when idle, so the first request is slow.
long_term: A good step up from free hosts once you need background workers.
watch_out: Free web services sleep after inactivity
Check the free database retention policy
Background workers are paid

name: Cloudflare R2
best_for: Object storage without egress fees
tradeoffs: S3-compatible storage with no egress fees, great for media-heavy apps. Fewer features than S3, and you design access control yourself.
long_term: Cheap to keep large files for years.
watch_out: Read and write operations are still charged
Use signed URLs for private files
Never expose bucket credentials in the browser

name: UploadThing
best_for: File uploads in a few lines
tradeoffs: File uploads in a few lines with typed helpers, ideal for React and Next apps. Another service with its own pricing and some SDK lock-in.
long_term: Plan an export path for stored files.
watch_out: Check storage and bandwidth limits
Files live on their infrastructure
SDK ties your upload flow to the service

name: PostHog
best_for: Product analytics and session replay
tradeoffs: Product analytics, session replay, feature flags and experiments in one place. Powerful but heavy to configure, and usage costs grow with events and recordings.
long_term: Pays off once you have real users to learn from.
watch_out: Control event volume
Mind privacy and cookie consent obligations
Mask sensitive fields in session replay

name: Plausible
best_for: Simple privacy-friendly traffic stats
tradeoffs: Lightweight, privacy-friendly traffic stats without cookies. Not a product analytics tool, and paid for hosted plans.
long_term: Open-source and self-hostable, with ops work if you do.
watch_out: Hosted pricing scales with pageviews
Not for detailed per-user analysis
Self-hosting means updates and backups

name: Sentry
best_for: Catch errors before users report them
tradeoffs: Catches front-end and back-end errors with stack traces and release tracking. A generous free tier, but event volume and performance monitoring add cost.
long_term: Install it before launch, not after the first outage.
watch_out: Scrub personal data from events
Set sampling rates to control cost
Filter noise from third-party scripts

name: Uptime Kuma
best_for: Self-hosted uptime monitor
tradeoffs: A free self-hosted monitor with a clean dashboard and many alert channels. If its own server goes down, your monitoring goes with it.
long_term: Run it on a different provider from the apps it watches.
watch_out: You maintain updates and backups
Host it separately from what it monitors
Test that alerts actually reach you

name: Paddle
best_for: Merchant of record for global software sales
tradeoffs: A merchant of record: Paddle sells to your customer and handles tax and compliance, which saves registrations. Fees are higher than a plain processor and businesses are reviewed before going live.
long_term: Suits software sold globally when you do not want to manage tax yourself.
watch_out: Check fee structure and which countries it pays out to
Approval review before you can sell
Fewer customization options than raw Stripe

name: Razorpay
best_for: UPI, cards and netbanking for businesses in India
tradeoffs: The usual gateway for Indian businesses, with UPI, cards, netbanking and wallets in one integration. Focused on India, so it is not a global solution.
long_term: Going live needs business verification in India, with settlement in rupees.
watch_out: Business verification (KYC) is required before live payments
Check international card acceptance and fees
Payment regulations in India change often

name: Mercado Pago
best_for: Local methods and wallets across Latin America
tradeoffs: Wide reach across Latin American markets with local payment methods and wallets. Accounts and features differ per country.
long_term: Choose the country account that matches your customers and currency.
watch_out: Methods and fees vary by country
Verify availability for your business country
Integration docs differ per market

name: Mollie
best_for: European payment methods with simple pricing
tradeoffs: Developer-friendly gateway with many European methods (iDEAL, Bancontact, SEPA, cards). Focused on Europe.
long_term: Best when most customers are in the EU or UK; less useful elsewhere.
watch_out: Check which business countries are supported
Method availability depends on the customer's country
Expect underwriting checks before going live
